research: Line move: SMU opened -6.5 and moved past the key number 7 by Monday to -9.5, mostly on Virginia's narrow win over Syracuse; Tuesday's Virginia injury news did not move it further (Predictem, Oct 16). A 3-point move means the number should be treated as fair; it doesn't favor either side.
[angle] Rest/travel: SMU is coming off a bye, while Virginia travels Friday for an 11 a.m. local kickoff in Dallas (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps SMU.
[angle] Virginia is 0-2 on the road this season, losing 38-7 at Florida State and to West Virginia in Charlotte; TeamRankings rates its road form among the worst (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps SMU.
[angle] Venue history: ACC teams are 0-9 against SMU in Dallas since 2024 (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps SMU, though it is old history.

Virginia injuries: CB Omillio Agard is out for the season (torn ACL), S Brandyn Hillman is a game-time decision (ankle), and WR Rico Flores Jr. and DE Devon Baxter are out (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps SMU.
SMU injuries: RB Dramekco Green is out 3-4 weeks (broken hand), and RB Christian Rhodes's debut after a hamstring issue is unconfirmed (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps Virginia.

Matchup: Virginia leads the ACC in pass defense and ranks about 2nd nationally in opponent dropback success rate, against SMU QB Kevin Jennings (about 75% completions) (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps Virginia.
Matchup: SMU ranks 107th against the run, and Virginia averages 163 rushing yards a game (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps Virginia.
Third downs and protection: SMU converts over half its third downs, while Virginia converts about 3 in 10 and allows 3+ sacks a game (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps SMU.
Margins: SMU's FBS games were decided by 3, 10 (a loss to Louisville), 10 and 9. It has rarely covered big numbers (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps Virginia at +9.5.
Ratings: SP+ has SMU about a 7-point favorite, while Game on Paper and TeamRankings rate the teams close to even (Predictem, Oct 16). Helps Virginia at +9.5.

Previews split: Predictem and Dimers took Virginia +9.5 (projected SMU 28-21 and 30-21), and SportsGambler took SMU -9.5 (projected 31-17) (search summaries, Oct 15-16). The model consensus leans Virginia, but that view is public information.
games.reasoning: This is a pass. The line moved 3 points through the key number 7, and the lessons say to treat a moved number as fair. Virginia's pass defense and SMU's weak run defense point one way, and Virginia's 0-2 road record, travel and SMU's bye point the other. The [angle] that stood out was SMU's bye against Virginia's Friday travel for an 11 a.m. local kickoff. A clear Hillman/Agard secondary collapse would have moved me toward SMU.
games.contaminationNote: While researching, I opened the Pickswise game page (pickswise.com/college-football/games/smu-virginia-college-football-2026-10-17-1200/picks/). It showed 'Final: SMU 23, Virginia 13'. I saw it before locking. My lean was already pass, formed from the 3-point move past 7 under the lessons, and I kept the pass.

research: Reverse line movement: Ohio State opened -4 and dropped to -3.5, repeatedly testing 3, even though Ohio State had about 80% of spread tickets and about 99% of spread money (WagerTalk/GoldSheet, Oct 14). The line moving against heavy Ohio State action helps Indiana, the underdog.
Moneyline move: Indiana moved from +160 to +150 despite public spread action, which the writer reads as sharp support for the Hoosiers (Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Indiana.

[angle] Indiana is getting points for the first time all season. Its 1-5 ATS mark came entirely as a favorite of 9.5 to 57 points (Predictem, Oct 14). The ATS record is mostly irrelevant as an underdog, which is mildly in Indiana's favor.

[angle] Ohio State's offensive line is reshuffled: Austin Siereveld is out for a 2nd straight game (Covers, Oct 17), and RT Phillip Daniels returns from about a month out. Ohio State's line ranks 75th in sacks allowed (Predictem, Oct 14). Indiana leads the Big Ten in sacks and TFL, with Daley and Osunsanmi at 5 sacks each. Helps Indiana.

Run matchup: Indiana ranks 6th in defensive rushing success rate and allows 2.6 yards per carry, while Ohio State ranks 81st in yards per rush (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14). Indiana held Ohio State to 58 rushing yards in the 2025 Big Ten title game (WagerTalk, Oct 14). Helps Indiana.

Efficiency: Indiana leads the nation at 7.6 yards per play, and Turbo Richard averages 8.4 yards per carry. Indiana has about one giveaway all season and 3.3 penalties a game, against Ohio State's 6.7 (Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Indiana.

Ohio State's strengths: it is 2nd nationally in EPA per pass, allows a nation-best 4.8 yards per pass, and Jeremiah Smith has 11 TD catches, while Indiana's defense ranks 76th in stopping pass EPA (Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Ohio State.

Ratings: ESPN FPI has Ohio State less than a point better, and SP+ has Ohio State 1st and Indiana 5th, under 3 points apart before home field. CollegeFootballRatings projects an Ohio State cover (Predictem, Oct 14). Roughly neutral to slightly in Indiana's favor at +3.5.

Form: Ohio State is 5-1, with its loss 23-24 to Texas and recent wins of 45-16 over Maryland and 31-14 over Iowa. Indiana is 6-0 but needed to rally from 11 down in the 4th quarter to win 20-17 at Nebraska and beat Northwestern only 29-23 (SportsGambler, Oct 15). Mildly helps Ohio State.

[angle] Ohio State has no reliable second receiver beside Jeremiah Smith, who had 11 catches against Iowa to 9 for the rest of the roster (WagerTalk, Oct 14). Indiana's pass rush can focus on a one-target passing game. Helps Indiana.
Cignetti is 6-2 SU and 5-3 ATS against top-10 opponents at Indiana (Covers, Oct 17). The tally is small, so this is a tiebreaker only.
Previews: WagerTalk, Predictem, Covers (Geoff Clark) and SportsGambler all took Indiana +3.5. Dimers' model projected Ohio State 26-23 (Oct 14-17).
games.reasoning: The deciding factor was the market. The line fell from 4 to 3.5 and Indiana's moneyline shortened despite about 80% of tickets and nearly all the money on Ohio State, which is reverse line movement toward the underdog, the one market sign that has held up. The [angle] that stood out was Ohio State's patched-together right side of the line facing the Big Ten's best pass rush. I shaded my projection back toward the line (Ohio State by about 1.5), so this is a lean, not strong. A move to Ohio State -4.5 or confirmation that Siereveld was back would have made it a pass.

research: Line move: Northwestern opened around -8.5, briefly hit -9.5, then was bet down to -7.5, with the writer reporting Michigan State drew the money and tickets that moved it (WagerTalk, Oct 14; Predictem, Oct 15). The slate has it at -7. That points to Michigan State support, so this helps Michigan State.

Ratings: SP+ has a nearly 17-point neutral-field gap, and Blue Chip makes Northwestern a 12.4-point favorite after Michigan State's home field (Predictem, Oct 15). Helps Northwestern, but this is public information the market moved away from.

Northwestern's offense averages 35.4 points per game, ranks 3rd in EPA per play and 4th in success rate, and gives up about half a turnover a game. Aidan Chiles completes 71.4% with no interceptions (Predictem, Oct 15). Helps Northwestern.

Michigan State's defense ranks 110th in EPA allowed, 126th in takeaways and 105th on third downs (Predictem, Oct 15). It has allowed 30+ points to 3 straight Big Ten opponents: Nebraska, Wisconsin and Illinois (WagerTalk, Oct 14). Helps Northwestern.

Recent results: Northwestern beat Penn State 34-13 and Ball State 45-14 and lost 23-29 to Indiana. Michigan State lost 3-31 at Wisconsin and 13-31 to Nebraska, then lost 37-38 in OT to Illinois (SportsGambler, Oct 15). Helps Northwestern.

[angle] Pat Fitzgerald coaches against Northwestern, where he won 110 games before his 2023 firing, for the first time. Northwestern's David Braun was his defensive coordinator (Predictem, Oct 15; WagerTalk, Oct 14). The emotional spot helps Michigan State.
[angle] Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles returns to face Michigan State, the team that benched him last November (Predictem, Oct 15). It cuts both ways, so it's neutral.

[angle] Northwestern has lost 4 straight Big Ten road games and has made only one other road trip this season. SportsGambler lists Northwestern 3-7 in its last 10 road games and says it hasn't covered -7.5 in 9 straight road games (Predictem, Oct 15; SportsGambler, Oct 15). Helps Michigan State, though old ATS trends are noise.

Michigan State's depth: RB Cam Edwards is out for the season, and several linebackers and corners were hurt against Illinois, though Fitzgerald said none are long-term. Its defense is described as thin (Predictem, Oct 15; WagerTalk, Oct 14). Helps Northwestern.
Northwestern's injuries: CB Josh Fussell is out and CB Braden Turner is questionable (Predictem, Oct 15). Michigan State QB Alessio Milivojevic completed 85% against Illinois. Helps Michigan State.
Rest: Michigan State is coming off an overtime game, while Northwestern had a low-stress win over Ball State (WagerTalk, Oct 14). Helps Northwestern.
Michigan State's run game averages 3.3 yards per carry (112th) (Predictem, Oct 15). Its path is through the air, which limits how it can control the clock as an underdog. Helps Northwestern.

Previews: Predictem projected Northwestern 33-20 and WagerTalk 34-23, both taking Northwestern -7.5. SportsGambler and Dimers took Michigan State +7.5. Covers' consensus was 58% on Northwestern (Oct 14-15).
games.reasoning: This is a pass. The efficiency gap (SP+ about 17) says Northwestern by double digits, but the market moved from -9.5 to -7 on Michigan State money, and the lessons say not to fight the line with ratings everyone has. The surprising [angle] was Fitzgerald's first game against the program he built, with his former coordinator on the other sideline, together with Northwestern's poor Big Ten road form. Shaded back toward the line, my projection lands within about 2 points of the key number 7, so I passed. A line back at 9+ or confirmed Michigan State defensive absences would have tipped it.

research: Line move: Texas opened about -9.5, moved to -10.5 (Predictem, Oct 15) and was -11.5 on game day (Covers and SportsGambler, Oct 17). The 2-point move toward Texas helps Texas.
Betting splits: Florida drew 41% of spread bets but 74% of the money (Predictem, Oct 15). The line still moved toward Texas, so the signals are mixed and neutral.

[angle] Florida is an underdog for the first time this season and has a bye before Georgia. It has lost two straight, 17-45 at Missouri and 19-38 to South Carolina (Predictem, Oct 15; SportsGambler, Oct 15). Its form helps Texas, and its lookahead to Georgia is unclear.

[angle] Texas has played three Power Four games, beating Ohio State 24-23 and Tennessee 20-17 and losing 24-27 to Oklahoma on a walk-off FG, all decided by 3 or fewer. Its offense hasn't pulled away from good teams (Predictem, Oct 15; SportsGambler, Oct 15). Helps Florida.
Texas's defense ranks 2nd in adjusted EPA per play, 9th against the run, 11th against the pass and 6th in defensive EPA per drive (Covers, Oct 17). Helps Texas.

Texas's offense ranks only 55th in success rate, 67th in EPA per pass and 70th in available yards (Covers, Oct 17). Arch Manning threw a pick-six and a late interception against Oklahoma (Predictem, Oct 15). Helps Florida.

Florida's defense ranks 123rd in success rate allowed (49.7%) and 136th in 3rd/4th-down success allowed, and it allows 292.8 passing yards a game. Its cornerback depth is described as thin (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 15). Helps Texas.
Florida's offense ranks 8th in EPA per pass at 6.4 yards per play, against Texas's 5.3, and SP+ ranks its special teams No. 1 (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 15). Helps Florida.
[angle] Pass rusher Colin Simmons (9.5 sacks) is a matchup problem for Florida's offense. Florida RB Jadan Baugh has only 72 rushing yards over the last two games (Predictem, Oct 15). Helps Texas.
Models: ESPN FPI has Texas by 16.6, CollegeFootballRatings by 13.8, and Dimers projects 31-19 (Predictem, Oct 15; Dimers). Helps Texas, but this is public information.
Texas is 1-4 ATS, with its only cover against Texas State (Predictem, Oct 15). ATS records are noise, so this is a tiebreaker only.
Weather: mostly sunny, low 60s, north wind about 10 mph (Covers, Oct 17). Neutral.
Previews split: Covers (Hatfield) took Texas -10.5 as a 'small edge' and would not go past it, while Predictem took Florida +10.5 with a projected 27-20 (Oct 15-17).
games.reasoning: This is a pass. Texas's elite defense against Florida's collapsing defense argues for a margin around the models' 14-17, but Texas's offense has won every Power Four game by 3 or fewer, and the number already moved 2 points toward Texas to 11.5. The [angle] that stood out was Texas going 0-for-3 at pulling away from good teams despite its defense. Shaded halfway back to the line, my projection sits about a point from the spread. A clear injury to a Florida offensive starter or Florida's QB would have pushed it toward Texas.

research: Line move: LSU opened -10.5 and moved to -14 at most books (-14.5 at FanDuel) (Predictem, Oct 14). It was -14.5 at Covers on game day (Covers, Oct 17), and Dimers listed -17.5 at one point. A 3.5+ point move on QB news means the number should be treated as fair, so this doesn't add to LSU.

[angle] Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor is questionable after aggravating a foot injury against Alabama that clearly limited him. Jeff Lebby planned a Wednesday decision, with Billy Puckett or AJ Swann as backups (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers, Oct 17). Status unresolved on game morning. It helps LSU, but the line move already counts it.
Leading rusher Fluff Bothwell is also questionable (foot), and WR Ayden Williams is out (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14). Helps LSU, but it is likely priced.

Mississippi State's offense ranks 5th in adjusted EPA per play, and Anthony Evans III leads the SEC at about 115 receiving yards a game (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14). That is with a healthy Taylor. It helps Mississippi State if he plays.

LSU's defense ranks 4th in adjusted EPA per play and 4th in EPA per pass allowed, allows 176 passing yards a game, gets nearly 4 sacks a game and allows a 34.1% passing success rate (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14). Helps LSU against a pass-first offense.
Mississippi State's defense ranks 101st in success rate allowed and 99th against the pass, and LSU runs for 214 yards a game (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14). Helps LSU.

LSU's offense is middling: 43rd in EPA per play and 63rd in rushing success rate. Sam Leavitt leads the SEC with 8 INTs, and Lane Kiffin called his team 'too up and down' in all phases (Covers, Oct 17; Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Mississippi State.

LSU's form: 4-0 at home, with wins over Clemson by 41 and Texas A&M by 29, and losses at Ole Miss and in OT at Kentucky (Predictem, Oct 14). Big home wins help LSU, and its uneven road form doesn't apply here.

Mississippi State's form: road wins at Minnesota and South Carolina, a win over Missouri, and 4-1 ATS, but it gave up 56 to Alabama at home last week (Predictem, Oct 14). Mixed. ATS records are noise.

Models: Cleatz has LSU -11.6, below the current number. Game on Paper's adjusted EPA gap (LSU 3rd, Mississippi State 24th) is worth about 12 points. Dimers projects 37-18 (Predictem, Oct 14; Dimers). The models built with a healthy Taylor sit near the opener, so they don't argue against the moved line.

[angle] The ESPN forecast calls for gusty wind in Baton Rouge (Predictem, Oct 14). It could hurt a pass-first Mississippi State offense, but per the lessons it is already priced into the total and spread. Neutral.
[angle] 14 is a push number (Predictem, Oct 14). Previews: Predictem LSU -14 (a 'solid lean' if Taylor is cleared, 35-17) and Covers LSU -14.5 (Oct 14-17).
games.reasoning: This is a pass. The line moved from 10.5 to 14 on Mississippi State's QB injury, so the lessons say to treat 14 as fair and not re-count Taylor's foot as a reason for LSU. His status was still unresolved on game morning and decides the game, which is itself a pass trigger. The [angle] that stood out was a top-5 EPA offense whose pass-first plan runs straight into LSU's top-5 pass defense with a hobbled QB in gusty wind. A confirmed backup QB start without a further line move would have pushed me toward LSU.

research: Line move: Texas Tech opened -12.5 and climbed to -14.5 at all books by Oct 14 (Predictem, Oct 14). It was -16.5 on game day (Covers, updated Oct 17, 12:37 PM ET, before the 3:30 kickoff). The market's closing number is 2 points beyond the slate's 14.5, so this helps Texas Tech at -14.5.

Ratings: SP+ rates Tech 18 points better on a neutral field before home field, and Action Network projects Tech -18.5 (Predictem, Oct 14). Dimers' model projects 33-16 (Dimers). Helps Texas Tech at -14.5.

Arizona State's offense ranks 106th in opponent-adjusted efficiency, with a weak passing game, and converts under 30% on third down (128th) (Predictem, Oct 14). Per the lessons, a big underdog needs to be able to score, so this helps Texas Tech.

Arizona State's results against good teams: lost 48-20 at Texas A&M as a two-TD underdog and 55-19 to Baylor. Its wins came over Kansas (in London), Hawaii (no cover) and Morgan State (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers, Oct 17). Helps Texas Tech.

Arizona State's defense allows 33 points a game (112th), nearly 390 yards a game and 145 rushing yards a game (Covers, Oct 17). Texas Tech runs for about 180 yards a game on about 39 carries and scores 35+ a game (Covers, Oct 17). Helps Texas Tech.

Texas Tech's defense ranks top-15 in SP+ and Game on Paper efficiency, has forced 7 turnovers in its last 2 games, and allows 2.3 points per trip inside the 40 (Predictem, Oct 14). It does rank 127th in pass yards allowed. Mostly helps Texas Tech.

[angle] Revenge: Arizona State's 26-22 win in Tempe last year was Tech's only regular-season loss. McGuire says his staff has a 'chip on our shoulder,' and the homecoming game is sold out (Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Texas Tech.
[angle] Rest: Texas Tech is 5-0 and coming off a bye. Arizona State's schedule included a London trip, and it had two weeks off before Baylor (Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Texas Tech.

[angle] Margin pattern: Tech has been close at halftime in 4 of 5 wins but is +72 after halftime (3rd nationally), so its covers come late. That gives Arizona State a backdoor risk only if it can score late (Predictem, Oct 14). Mixed, leaning Texas Tech.

Texas Tech's injuries: RB Cam Dickey is out (ankle), so J'Koby Williams, Quinten Joyner and freshman Ace Rowden carry the load. QB Will Hammond has 5 TD passes and 5 INTs, so his turnovers could give Arizona State short fields (Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Arizona State.
Arizona State's line gets healthier: starting C Tana Alo-Tupuola and RG Wade Helton return for QB Cutter Boley (Predictem, Oct 14). Helps Arizona State.

Tech is 2-3 ATS this season, including a 2-point escape against Houston as a 7.5-point favorite, and 8-5 ATS in its last 13 (Predictem, Oct 14; Covers, Oct 17). ATS records are noise, so this is a tiebreaker only.
Weather: mid-50s, little wind (Covers, Oct 17). Neutral. Previews: Predictem Tech -14.5, playable to -16.5 (31-14), and Covers Tech -16.5 (both Oct 14-17).
games.reasoning: The deciding factor was the market. Tech moved from -12.5 to -16.5 by game day, and SP+ plus home field (about 21) and Action Network (-18.5) sit above the slate's 14.5, so this side is 2 points better than the closing number rather than a bet into the moved line. Arizona State's 106th-ranked offense, which converts under 30% on third down, gives little backdoor path. The [angle] was revenge for Tech's only regular-season loss last year, coming off a bye. A Hammond-led turnover game is the risk; if the slate number had matched the -16.5 close, this would have been a pass.
